us-equities.title: Portfolio and risk
us-equities.verdict_overturn_when: The verdict changes if an executed comparison on the same frozen inputs, blueprints/us-equities/research-evaluation/plan.json with the hash-locked requirements.lock, shows either of these: (a) cvxportfolio's multi-period cost-aware policy, or empyrical-reloaded or quantstats metrics, produce reproducible, independently recomputed portfolio or risk outputs that the skfolio path lacks; or (b) a skfolio optimizer or risk estimator fails native acceptance. That comparison needs a recorded run of blueprints/us-equities/research-evaluation/evaluate.py extended with those arms, plus 'python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_research_evaluation.py -q' passing. A regression of that focused test below 12 passed would also reopen the verdict.

winners.why_selected: skfolio (c3) is the only adopted candidate with retained native execution evidence, but that evidence covers one function: the WalkForward splitter. It does not cover the layer's portfolio-optimization, performance-evaluation or legacy-metrics scope terms, and no candidate has native evidence for those. blueprints/us-equities/research-evaluation/evaluate.py:181-183 is the only place skfolio is used. It imports skfolio.model_selection.WalkForward and requires installed version 1.2.9. The receipt (kind "native_cli_e2e", status "accepted_for_causal_raw_price_label_control_only", observed_utc 2026-09-19T22:59:04Z) records WalkForward 252/63/6 with reduce_test=True on Python 3.13.15. The run produced 20 development folds, 21 frozen selections and 6605 candidate records. Its recorded acceptance commands are "focused-tests" (python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_research_evaluation.py -q; exit 0, "12 passed") and "full-tests" (exit 0, "214 passed, 0 skipped"), at receipt.json lines 1562-1589. The receipt's independent review reports 42 private artifact hashes verified with 0 mismatches. README.md says: "This accepts the splitter used here, not every skfolio optimizer." The same file says the labels are not portfolio P&L. The packet's external c3 ref is the v1.2.8 README, while the pin and the executed wheel are 1.2.9. catalogs/us-equities/engines-strategies.md:85 reconciles the two as "1.2.9 accepted splitter; 1.2.8 earlier review". This verdict departs from the repository's catalog ranking. engines-strategies.md:82 makes quantstats the Default and :85 makes skfolio "Conditional beyond accepted scope". The packet withheld those decisions, and I rank c3 first only because it alone has observed execution. This is a narrow winner, not proof of fitness for the whole layer. quantstats (c4) is kept as a conditional complement for reporting.

alternatives.name: data-edgartools
alternatives.why_not_default: Revised from winner. The edgartools-specific native evidence is index acquisition only. In access-resolution.json lines 31-56, edgar.get_filings(2020,1,form='8-K',amendments=True,filing_date='2020-03-02') plus to_context exited 0 with HTTP 200. It returned an 8-K/8-K/A cohort of 371 rows for filing date 2020-03-02 (360 unique accessions; 8-K 362, 8-K/A 9; 5 context rows), taken from the full QTR1 form.gz (5079824 bytes compressed, 50685481 decompressed). The 371 rows are that filtered cohort, not the size of the Q1 index. The historical rejection (eligible_count 0, before_first_availability 5 at as-of 2020-03-03T00:00:00Z; lines 104-111) came from 'catalyst.py packet'. That is custom repository code: line 15 says the source/provenance bridge is custom repository code, and catalyst.py lines 3-16 use only the standard library, including urllib on the daily master index. The exclusion reason is first observation by this runtime in 2026, not dissemination lag. The earlier receipt.json keeps the 403 and quarantined-fixture failure. edgartools is a qualified SEC acquisition source for filing-derived factors, but its output has not been shown feeding any point-in-time factor or evaluation run.

The run recorded 21 frozen selections and 6605 ledger records (receipt line 1379). The audit records all_training_exits_before_evaluation_cutoff true and all_observed_decision_before_entry_before_exit true. The hash-locked install passed uv pip check. The full suite reported 214 passed, 0 skipped (lines 1578-1589). An independent review, status accepted, verified the artifact and selection hashes. These counts are copied from the receipt as documented results; I did not observe them now. skfolio's own contribution is narrower than the run: evaluate.py line 181 imports WalkForward and line 210 builds the splitter, so skfolio supplied only the index splits. The 6-row purge equals the declared 6-session label exit horizon (plan.json lines 15, 18, 25). The reserved outcome is weak: the selected momentum20 had mean_net_cost_proxy_label 0.001184071666615635470939591764, below the equalweight control at 0.001622928696130345656850000132 and below momentum60/momentum120 at 0.004403128517506842397527919636 (receipt lines 1392-1437). c23 is selected as the natively exercised chronological-validation component, not as proof of any signal. c11 (edgartools) was dropped from the winner set in revision. alternatives.name: Pandera
alternatives.why_not_default: Pandera has a retained fail-closed schema gate (data/promotion_gate.py lines 148-180 and 232-273), but it has run only on synthetic CSV fixtures (data/README.md lines 70-73). fixtures/good-gate-result.json records pass with 12 checks and row_count 4. fixtures/bad-gate-result.json records fail on valid_trading_session, volume_integral_non_negative, observed_at_not_future, high_ge_max_open_close and unique_symbol_session, with row_count 4. Both record pandera 0.33.1. The packet's evidence_refs list the upstream README only, and the gate's duckdb:// input path is source-only because duckdb is not in the gate venv (promotion_gate.py lines 13-16). Fail-closed rejection on real data in this layer is demonstrated by DuckDB SQL instead: coverage.py lines 484-502 and eligibility_gates over 24195741 candidate rows (broad-universe/receipt.json lines 1097-1099). Pandera becomes a co-winner if the gate runs fail-closed on a real DuckDB-produced snapshot.

alternatives.name: data-arrow
alternatives.why_not_default: pyarrow 25.0.1 appears only as a version field in the gate results. The gate read CSV fixtures, not Parquet (data/README.md lines 70-73). DuckDB wrote and reread the retained Parquet itself (summarize_backtest.py lines 25-26; coverage.py lines 521-523). I found no retained Arrow-specific check of precision or time-unit roundtrip, which the card's own limitation requires. The upstream README was not opened.

alternatives.why_not_default: The only packet evidence is the upstream README URL, which was not opened. The packet marks the pin v26.8.7.19-lts as behind upstream v26.9.2.8-stable. Eventual merges must not be treated as an immutable revision ledger.

alternatives.why_not_default: Native CLI execution exists, but for serialization rather than storage/compute. toon-encode and toon-decode both exited 0, with toon_roundtrip_equal true, in evidence/receipts/portable-cli-artifacts.json. component-history.json says native_claude and native_codex use is 'not independently demonstrated'. alternatives.why_not_default: Source review only; the README URL was not opened. No feature-store execution is retained. The card says event-time point-in-time retrieval does not exclude late corrections, and that materialization freshness and skew need separate operational evidence.

alternatives.why_not_default: Not adopted, with empty packet evidence_refs and card_limitations. Its note makes it conditional on a curated research database, a read-only principal and max_rows enforcement, and none of these is retained. It is an access layer, not storage or compute.

open_gaps: Historical as-known availability of market data is not established. The broad-universe collection uses 'asof': 'provider default (request date)' (broad-universe/receipt.json line 90). The only retained rejection of records not yet available at the as-of date is on SEC metadata: catalyst-dataset/native-receipt.json line 87 records 0 eligible headers as of 2020-03-03.

Corporate-action coverage is incomplete. The receipt says coverage 'is thin before 2020, so names delisted in 2016-2019 without a retained action remain undiscoverable', and that the provider asset list under-enumerates delisted names (broad-universe/receipt.json line 334). Rename-pair de-duplication is implemented (coverage.py lines 484-493), but full adjustment reconciliation is not; the packet limitations cite missing dividend currency.

No comparative throughput or concurrency measurement exists. The only figure is one DuckDB elapsed time, 71.138 s (broad-universe/receipt.json line 1073), so the server, lake and distributed candidates (c2, c3, c5, c6) remain untested, not failed.

The Pandera gate has run only on 4-row synthetic CSV fixtures. Its duckdb:// input path is untested source code (promotion_gate.py lines 13-16), and it does not check corporate actions, as-known availability or provider completeness.
No retained check is dedicated to Arrow/Parquet precision or time-unit roundtrip under pyarrow.
Licensing and redistribution terms for the SIP feed are not established by the evidence I read. The receipt states 'real entitled provider data' but retains no rights terms.

overturn_protocol.metric: On one frozen, representative real snapshot, measure five things: exact DECIMAL/timestamp roundtrip equality; seeded-defect rejection that fails closed with no silent pass; a byte-identical Parquet hash on rebuild; local query latency/concurrency at the required universe size; and zero skipped tests in each pinned environment.

us-equities.overturn_when: Freeze required universe/history/latency, rights, correction and availability semantics; compare selected providers on representative securities including delistings, ticker reuse and corporate actions, then change the feed/store only when a candidate closes those gaps with auditable records and acceptable measured cost. Add a server or lake only after local throughput/concurrency measurements justify it.
us-equities.title: Storage and compute
us-equities.verdict_overturn_when: Any of three results would change this verdict. (1) The DuckDB checks stop passing with zero skips when each suite runs in its own pinned environment: run `python3 -m unittest tests.test_financial_data` with the research interpreter where duckdb is importable (skipUnless at tests/test_financial_data.py lines 229 and 246), and run `python3 -m unittest tests.test_promotion_gate` with the gate venv present (skipUnless at tests/test_promotion_gate.py line 90). A skip-only pass does not count. (2) Rerunning blueprints/us-equities/broad-universe/coverage.py on the retained ledger fails to reproduce the recorded row totals (24195741 rows in contract) or does not fail closed on duplicate (symbol, session_date) rows. (3) An executed, frozen comparison on a representative real snapshot, including delistings, ticker reuse and corporate actions, shows that ClickHouse, QuestDB or Iceberg/PyIceberg beats DuckDB. The comparison would measure exact DECIMAL/timestamp roundtrip, seeded-defect rejection, byte-identical snapshot rebuilds, and local throughput/concurrency at the required universe size. Pandera (c8) becomes a co-winner when blueprints/us-equities/data/promotion_gate.py runs fail-closed on a real DuckDB-produced snapshot with seeded defects.

winners.why_selected:
c4 DuckDB is the only candidate in the storage/compute role with retained native execution. c10 TOON also has native CLI execution, but its role is serialization of model context. My own source review found four DuckDB receipts.
(1) blueprints/us-equities/broad-universe/receipt.json records real entitled provider data (line 6: 'measured on real entitled provider data (read-only GETs)'). The plan uses feed 'sip', timeframe 1Day, 2016-01-01 to 2026-09-18 and 15418 symbols (lines 72-90). It collected 24310292 raw bars in 2554 pages, and the csv and ledger totals match (lines 22-57). The page sha256 re-verification shows 5108/5108 verified and 0 mismatches (lines 65-71). In broad-universe/coverage.py, DuckDB fails closed when the corporate-action ledger is incomplete or no rename pair loads (lines 484-493) and when duplicate (symbol, session_date) rows exist (lines 497-502). It then writes ZSTD Parquet and rereads the row count (lines 521-523). The evaluation ran duckdb_version 1.5.5 with elapsed_s 71.138, produced an events.parquet of 3532983 rows, used 24195741 bars and recorded 0 off-calendar rows. The eligibility gates covered 24195741 candidate rows (receipt lines 1070-1099).
(2) blueprints/us-equities/data/receipt.json (native_cli_e2e) records DuckDB (duckdb==1.5.5, workers/requirements.txt line 4) projecting 6 native LEAN simulated order events to DECIMAL(20,8), writing ZSTD Parquet and rereading it (summarize_backtest.py lines 19-28). The result was 3 distinct orders, 3 filled and 3 submitted, with parquet_sha256 48ec550a.... The Dagu order_table step (research-runtime/prepare-evidence.yaml lines 9-11) re-ran summarize_backtest.py on a fresh LEAN order-events file. It produced the same parquet_sha256 (research-runtime/receipt.json line 53), which shows a byte-identical rebuild, not the Parquet being passed downstream.
(3) catalyst-dataset/native-receipt.json line 89 records repeat_parquet_bytes_identical true. Line 87 shows historical as_of 2020-03-03 returning 0 eligible headers, so DuckDB rejected records not yet available at that date.
(4) financial-data/receipt.json offline_verification records an exact DECIMAL(38,12) roundtrip, but on artificial fixtures only.
Pandera (c8) is not a co-winner. Its only retained runs are on 4-row synthetic CSVs, and the real-data rejection evidence in this layer is DuckDB's.
